FACT [D-02 `price`]: "date": "2025-06-26", "series": "raw", value 12600 minor USD. FACT [D-02 `value_per_share`]: 1596 minor USD; [D-02 `band`]: "low" 1076, "high" 2250 minor USD across twelve cells spanning discount rates 8–11% and terminal growth 1.5–3.5%. INFERENCE (from these two): no combination of discount rate and terminal growth in the grid reaches the traded price, so the conclusion does not turn on either — it turns on the base cash flow and the growth required from it.

FACT [D-02 `implied`]: "solves_for": "stage1_growth", "status": "SOLVED", "value": "0.282629394532", residual 0. FACT [annual history, metric `fcff`]: FY2016 −2,403,000,000; FY2020 −69,209,856; FY2023 −6,325,000,000; FY2024 −354,404,839 USD, with FY2017–FY2019 and FY2021–FY2022 positive. INFERENCE (from these two): the price asks for ten consecutive years of ~28% FCFF compounding from a company whose nine measured years contain four negative readings and five sign changes; the longest positive run in the record is three years.

FACT [10-Q]: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range." FACT [10-Q MD&A]: nine-month DRAM sales rose "primarily due to a high-40% range increase in average selling prices"; gross margin "38%" against "37%", "27%" and "17%" in the other disclosed periods. INFERENCE (from these two): the cash flow being compounded is struck on a price move above the top of the company's own published five-year band, and on the highest margin in the filing's record.

FACT [10-Q MD&A, sequential]: DRAM showed "a low-single-digit percent range decrease in average selling prices" and NAND "a high-single-digit percent range decrease"; FACT [10-Q segment]: "SBU | (9) | (1)%". INFERENCE: the price variable has already turned sequentially in both product lines while the year-over-year rate still reads high.

**The caveat that does most of the work against my own verdict.** FACT [D-02 `basis.inputs`]: quarterly capex of 312,000,000,000 / 320,600,000,000 / 405,500,000,000 / 293,800,000,000 minor USD against operating cash flow of 340,500,000,000 / 324,400,000,000 / 394,200,000,000 / 460,900,000,000 minor USD, producing base_fcff of 134,944,285,145 minor USD. FACT [10-Q]: "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion"; "Construction in progress(2) 4,937 | 3,444"; "costs related to equipment not placed into service of $3.40 billion"; "first DRAM wafer output projected in the second half of calendar 2027". FACT [ca.capex, status not_found]: "the company makes no maintenance/growth split anywhere in the filing." INFERENCE (from these): the base charges in full capital spending whose output arrives after the base period, so a maintenance-only base would be higher and the required growth lower — and the bundle supplies no split with which to size the difference. ASSUMPTION (mine, rejectable independently): I treat the gross-capex basis as the right measure of current owner cash; a reader who treats the ~$14bn programme as predominantly growth should treat the valuation gap as materially smaller and undetermined by this bundle.

**Two corroborations I decline to use.** FACT [J-20 `derived.basis`]: normalised cycle_average_fcff 128,727,406,636 minor USD, close to D-02's base; FACT [J-20 `derived.basis.provenance`]: "exclusions_applied": false. INFERENCE: that figure is an unadjusted nine-year mean of a series containing four negative years, not a normalised base, so it corroborates D-02 less than J-09 claimed. FACT [J-14]: the finance-lease liability sits inside D-02 `net_debt.components` under "LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations" (1,500,300,000,000 minor USD) and "DebtCurrent" (53,800,000,000 minor USD), and J-11's comparison of $1,247m of lease additions to the "$1.35bn TTM FCFF base" runs the wrong way arithmetically. INFERENCE: the strongest Stage C bear reason is weaker than stated, and I do not carry it.

**What I cannot say.** INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: the consensus estimate set, rating record, peer figures or a reference-class base rate as published on 2025-06-26. why: FACT [declared absent inputs]: consensus forward estimates "cannot be reconstructed", rating actions "NOT fetched", "peer_set_figures: no peer or industry part kind exists", "reference_class_base_rates: the bundle is single-company", "market_capitalisation: no D-02 output computes it". would_change: if consensus implied growth near 28%, I would be differing from the market on a measurable requirement; if it implied cycle-average growth, the price would be the outlier to both of us and the gap would be a market-structure question rather than an analytical one. Separately, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on leverage headroom — FACT [dm.headroom, not_found]: the filing "discloses no computed actual ratio, no adjusted EBITDA figure, and no statement of compliance" against a covenant "not to exceed 3.25 to 1.00".

**The one observation that would move me to the adjacent position:** a disclosure splitting maintenance from growth capital expenditure — or two quarters of capex below $2.5bn with gross profit intact — would move this from "the price is unsupported by any basis in the bundle" to "the price is unsupported only on a gross-capex basis, and the correct basis is not in the bundle.""}
